$comment: Seeded design faults: realistic single-point bugs injected into a COPY of the canonical RTL drop, one at a time, to measure whether the whole validation stack (monitors, harness, generated SVA, coverage sampling, scoreboard, checkers) detects them and blames the right block. Each fault is a literal text substitution that must match the block's RTL exactly once — a mutation that does not apply is an error, never a silent pass. `expect` names the detectors that should fire, in the signature vocabulary of seed_faults.py: id:<taxonomy or rule id>, assert:<generated assertion label>, illegal:<coverpoint>, stage:<stage name> (a stage newly failing), matched:<stage> (an exact stage matching fewer transactions), log:<marker>. Detection is DIFFERENTIAL against the baseline reports of the same drop, because the drop is already broken: a fault is killed only when a detector appears that the baseline did not show, or an expected detector's count grows.

faults.description: ACTIVATE always targets bank 0 (bank field dropped on the DDR pins).
ACTIVATE is driven with the PRECHARGE pin encoding.

tRAS timer loaded with 1 instead of the configured value; PRECHARGE follows ACTIVATE too early. (Replaces a tRCD fault that was equivalent: at this clock tRCD is 3 cycles and the ACT->CAS pipeline is structurally longer, so no timer bug can violate it.)
faults.reseeded: 2026-09-24: block rewritten in the Frontend2 drop (c8ac792); same fault, new site

faults.description: tRRD timer never loaded; ACTIVATEs to different banks may be back-to-back. (Replaces a tRC fault that was equivalent: tRC = tRAS + tRP, and both are enforced separately, so a broken tRC timer alone cannot produce a violation.)
faults.reseeded: 2026-09-24: block rewritten in the Frontend2 drop (c8ac792); same fault, new site

faults.description: The tREFI tick is never raised; no refresh is ever requested.
An acknowledge increments the postpone counter instead of decrementing it.
TIMING_0 resets to a value one off the spec's reset value.

RW1C flag becomes settable by a bus write (write-1 sets instead of clears). (Replaces a lost-latch fault that was unobservable: the starvation event is unreachable in this RTL, see the ref_pending_cnt width finding.)
faults.reseeded: 2026-09-24: block rewritten in the Frontend2 drop (c8ac792); same fault, new site

faults.description: Bank bits taken from the wrong address slice.
Write-enable inverted on the internal request.

Row address stored inverted on enqueue. (Detected only after SCHED_004 — ACTIVATE row must correspond to a pending request — was added to the stage rules and the checker regenerated: the first draft of the suite found a rule gap, not an RTL gap.)
Row conflicts are never resolved: the PRECHARGE branch is unreachable.
faults.masked_by: scheduler_regrant (open): the baseline already drops requests (19 enqueued, 16 dequeued) through the slot re-grant defect, so this fault's dropped requests add 3 to a count that is already non-zero. Re-testable once that defect is fixed.

faults.description: DDR data mask driven with host byte-enable polarity (not inverted).
faults.masked_by: data_path_width (open): the design drives 32-bit beats where the spec's pack_32_to_16 predicts 16-bit halves, so every write beat already mismatches on data; a mask-only change cannot alter the verdict. Re-testable once that defect is fixed.

faults.description: Init sequence skips MR2 (goes straight to MR3).
faults.reseeded: 2026-09-24: block rewritten in the Frontend2 drop (c8ac792); same fault, new site

faults.description: cal_done asserted without waiting for init_done.

$equivalent_note: Three first-draft faults were 'equivalent mutants' — unobservable by construction, not missed by a check: tRCD/tRP timer bugs cannot violate a 3-cycle bound the command pipeline already exceeds, and the refresh-starvation latch never fires because the event is unreachable in this RTL. They were replaced; the reasoning is kept in each replacement's description.
$lessons: Stimulus: the first run left 8 faults alive because random host addresses were capped at 63 (bank 0, row 0 forever). Fixed in closure/random_sequence.py; four faults died immediately. A detection rate is only as good as the stimulus reaching the fault.

Rule gap: M11 (row corrupted in the queue) was invisible until SCHED_004 (ACTIVATE row must correspond to a pending request) was added to the stage rules and the checkers regenerated. The suite found a hole in the checks, which is its purpose.

Scorer vocabulary: M12 was detected by the checker (request_not_serviced) but not recognised because the scorer only matched taxonomy-style ids. Violation lines now lead with the taxonomy id and the scorer accepts any rule token.

Equivalent mutants: tRCD/tRP timer bugs cannot violate a 3-cycle bound the command pipeline already exceeds; tRC = tRAS + tRP so a tRC-only bug cannot show; the starvation latch never fires because the event is unreachable. Replaced with tRAS, tRRD and an RW1C-settable fault.

M04 (tRRD zero) was caught by the tFAW window assertion rather than tRRD: with no tRRD hold-off the fifth ACTIVATE lands inside tFAW first. M06 (postpone runaway) was caught by tRFC rather than REF_001: the REF_001 checker compares against the SPEC's max_postpone_count while the refresh-stress stimulus reprograms the CSR to 2 — the checker should observe cfg_refresh. Filed as a checker to-do.
Masked faults (M12, M13) are re-tested automatically when the masking defect closes: the scorer reports them apart and never counts them as kills.
$todo: cmd_queue_scheduler / scheduler / path_05 / path_20 checkers should take cfg_refresh as an input stream so REF_001 uses the programmed postpone budget, not the spec constant.
$reseed_note: Fault sites are literal text; when a block is regenerated the site moves. Check applicability with tests/test_seed_faults.py before trusting a matrix.
